text.56_Daf, 0_Comment: Passage: "The friend and the enemy, who is a friend? This is his groomsman." And we asked: How long must one celebrate with him to be called his groomsman? Ravina said in the name of R. Yirmiyah bar Abba who said in the name of Rav: All seven days of the feast. But less than that, he is not called a groomsman and is not disqualified as a friend. But the Rabbis said in the name of Rava: Even from the first day he is called a groomsman and is disqualified according to R. Yehuda's reasoning. Some interpret it thus: How long is he disqualified? Ravina said: All seven days of the feast, but after that he is valid. And the Rabbis who disagree with R. Yehuda — what is their view? Rav said: Even from the first day he is valid to testify. But this interpretation is not correct: Since the Rabbis state definitively "Jews are not suspected of this," why would we need to ask anything regarding the Rabbis? He is certainly valid always. Furthermore, how can Rava say "even from the first day" — which implies from the first day onward — suggesting that on the first day at least he is disqualified? This means the Rabbis recognize a disqualifying friendship, and they only disagree about the measure. But then according to the Rabbis too, Jews would be suspected of this in some way. Yet the Mishnah does not teach this; rather, Jews are not suspected of this at all. Moreover, what is the meaning of "even"? It would surely be more appropriate to disqualify him on the seventh day than the first, since his affection has not yet grown so close. Therefore, this interpretation is certainly incorrect.
